newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar touch weaker in very thin trade.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar touch weaker in very thin trade.

text.p: London's white sugar futures market was extremely quiet on Monday morning and showed little desire to stir into life before the open of the New York raws market.
Trading was confined to just 18 lots of the two nearby contracts by 1112 GMT, both of which were marginally lower.
October was down 80 cents at $326.50 and December down 30 cents at $322.50.
Technical analysts said a renewed upwards push was possible given that October appeared to have staged a sufficient correction and was holding above $325.
Initial resistance was pegged at $329, followed by $331 and $335.
Traders complained that fresh physical news was thin on the ground although Syria is slated to re-tender this week to buy 13,000 tonnes of whites and 13,000 of raws.
Tuesday is set as the final date to receive price offers with the two amounts to be shipped in September.
Just 18 lots of spot October were traded in Paris. The contract was down $1.10 at $326.10. Nothing was traded on the 100 ICUMSA market.
